title: Monica's tears (Confessions 3)
hook: a mother prays for years for her son; a bishop tells her a son of such tears can't be lost

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ambrose and the emperor, and his paenitentia: a private letter, King David's words, and an emperor who laid aside his rank. Your line was even the emperor. What true thing did you say? Day seven hundred thirty-three.

Augustine wrote his Confessions talking to God, not to us. We're overhearing. And in the third book he remembers his mother, crying. He's a young man, brilliant, restless, and he has joined a religious movement called the Manichees, whose teaching he later left behind. His mother, Monica, is a Christian, and she weeps over him. He says she wept for him more than mothers weep over a child's dead body. He's writing this long afterward, and he sets her tears down in a book addressed to God.
screen: `A BOOK WRITTEN TO GOD.` → `A SON GONE ANOTHER WAY.` → `A MOTHER WHO WEEPS.`

segments.voice: Augustine tells two moments. First, a dream. Monica dreams she's standing on a wooden ruler, grieving, and a young man, bright and smiling, comes up and asks why she's sad. She says she's mourning her son's ruin. He tells her to look: where she is, there her son is too. She looks, and sees Augustine standing beside her on the same ruler. When she tells him, Augustine tries to twist it. Maybe it means she'll come round to where he is. She answers straight away: no. It didn't say where he is, you are. It said where you are, he is. Augustine admits that her quick answer moved him more than the dream did. Second, a bishop. Augustine doesn't name him. Monica begs this bishop to talk with her son and argue him out of his errors. The bishop refuses. The young man is too pleased with his new ideas, he says. Let him alone. Only pray for him. He'll find out by reading. The bishop even tells her he went down that same road as a boy, and found his own way out. But Monica keeps pressing, and crying. And finally, a little annoyed, the bishop says the line Augustine wrote down. Go your way, he tells her: it cannot be that the son of these tears should be lost. Augustine says she took it as if it had sounded from heaven. Notice what the bishop didn't do. He didn't argue with the son. He sent the mother back to her prayers.
screen: `A DREAM OF A WOODEN RULER.` · `WHERE YOU ARE, THERE HE IS.` · `LET HIM ALONE. ONLY PRAY.` · `THE SON OF THESE TEARS.` · then, large: `IT CANNOT BE THAT HE SHOULD BE LOST.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for someone who's far away. Settle, and breathe. Bring one person to mind who feels far from you right now. Far in miles, or far in some other way: gone quiet, gone another direction. Don't argue with them in your head. Just hold them. Say their name. If you pray, you can place them before God the way Monica did. If you don't, keep them in mind, warmly, without fixing anything. The bell holds the time.
Monica's tears. A mother's prayers for her son Augustine, and a bishop's promise that the son of such tears could not be lost. Today's word.
Your line: the son of these tears. Today, send one kind word to someone far away, with no argument attached. Day seven hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Monica as a saint and some ask her prayers for children who have drifted from the faith; her feast falls the day before her son Augustine's.

original.note: Latin: the son of these tears — the bishop's words to Monica in the Confessions.

trapdoor: what you thought: a mother nagged her son back to church.
what it means: she prayed and wept, and a bishop told her not to argue him back but to let him alone and pray.
what a scholar hears: Confessions 3.11–12 in Augustine's Latin: the dream of the wooden rule, and fieri non potest, ut filius istarum lacrimarum pereat.

sources.quoted: fieri non potest, ut filius istarum lacrimarum pereat

notes: Confessions 3.11.19–20 paraphrased: Monica's weeping 'more than mothers weep the bodily deaths of their children'; the dream of the wooden rule (regula) and the radiant youth; 'where you are, there he is'; Augustine's twisted reading and her correction; her answer moving him more than the dream. Confirm. 'Ruler' is used for regula in the voice; scholar may prefer 'rule' or 'measuring rod'.

Confessions 3.12.21 paraphrased: the unnamed bishop, his refusal ('let him alone; only pray'), his own past among the Manichees, and the line. Latin quoted from the original: confirm 'fieri non potest, ut filius istarum lacrimarum pereat'. The English 'it cannot be that the son of these tears should be lost' is the script's own rendering, not quoted from a translation.
Manichees described neutrally as a religious movement Augustine later left. Confirm the framing is fair.
howItsDone: feasts of St. Monica (Aug. 27) and St. Augustine (Aug. 28) in the Roman calendar; the script says only 'the day before'. Confirm.
Editor pass: replaced the hook's guess at Augustine's motive ('he wants God to know he noticed') with what the text does: he sets her tears down in a book addressed to God.
Audit pass: checked against Confessions 3.11.19–3.12.21 and the Latin line; no error found, no change.
